messages:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency alert for single-tenant customer 'valencia-health' on dedicated-nyc-1. Threshold breach: p99 > 3s for streaming responses. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream. Incident ID: INC-3034567890 :rotating_light:

oncall-amber: acked, I'm on it. grabbing traces + routing table now. @sre-raj you'll want to look at node pool allocations.

sre-raj: seeing large tail at 21:04:12 UTC. p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 3.4s. spike correlates with a small set of sessions from valencia: session_ids: [sess_8a2, sess_8a3]. logs show repeated long prefixes and many emoji tokens. possible KV-cache thrash.

eng-runtime-mia: can you paste a sample of the offending prompt? if it's long-runner prefix we may be evicting KV entries frequently.

support-ash: pulled a redacted prompt from customer chat (valencia contact Delia):
```
User: "\ud83d\ude0d\ud83e\udd70 [long medical note repeated 8x] please summarize with bullets and timeline. Also include provenance and citations."
```
It's got a long repeated section + lots of emoji and HTML-ish markup. length ~ 18k chars.

eng-ml-luke: that matches a pattern we've seen where the model's attention window + repeated prefix causes the runtime to rebuild KV frequently, especially under concurrency. which model are they pinned to?

oncall-amber: valencia pinned to rdx-foresight-11b (q4fy) on dedicated-nyc-1. 6 active connections at the spike time.

eng-runtime-mia: ok that model + long prefix + concurrent sessions = KV cache churn. log snippet from node-32 at 21:04:11:
```
WARN kvcache: eviction cycle start, active_keys=12870, memory=78%
INFO runtime: clear_kv_chunk node-32 seq=4412 prefix_hash=0x3f8b2
DEBUG rpc: stream_chunk_reordered session=sess_8a2 latency=512ms
```
We also see continuous batching intervals extending to 210ms (normally 50-70ms).

sre-raj: network latencies between frontend and node-32 are normal. CPU/GPU metrics show GPU utilization moderate (~62%) but memory pressure on host is high. I think it's in-memory metadata for the KV cache.

pm-jordan: customer impact? are they seeing errors or only higher latency?

support-ash: only higher latency and streaming stalls; no 5xxs. customer reported degraded UX on long summaries. they escalated to support at 21:05. Delia on the thread: "we're getting very laggy outputs and some streams hang halfway through, not timing out though".

eng-ml-luke: short-term mitigations we can consider now: 1) apply per-customer request rate limiting to 10rps for valencia, 2) route valencia to smaller model variant (rdx-foresight-6b) temporarily, 3) enable prefix-truncation on gateway for >8k chars, 4) bump KV cache size for node-32 if possible.

eng-runtime-mia: I can push a routing override to send new requests to rdx-fore-6b with degraded QoS tag. doing canary 1/1 now. command:
```
# routing override
redwoodctl routes update --customer valencia-health --route /v1/chat/stream --model rdx-fore-6b --reason "mitigate-kvcache-thrash-3034567890"
```
Applying... done. new requests should start hitting 6b in ~10s.

oncall-amber: enabled per-customer throttling (burst 20, sustained 10rps).

sre-raj: bumped node-32 kvcache limit by +15% via infra flag, restart avoided using hot-config.

incident-bot: Note: Canary routing change detected: valencia-health -> rdx-fore-6b (canary 1/1).

eng-ml-luke: monitoring p99 now. initial drop seen: p99 before = 3.4s, after routing/limit = 980ms within 30s. p95 stable ~ 450ms. streaming stall counts reduced.

support-ash: told Delia we've applied mitigations and are monitoring. they'll confirm if UX improves.

customer-delia-valencia: Thanks team, looks much better for the next couple of sessions. still seeing one stalled stream at 21:09 but overall faster. appreciate the fast response. :pray:

eng-runtime-mia: re: root cause: KV cache eviction thrash caused by very long repeated prefixes plus multiple concurrent sessions pinned to 11b. cache metadata growth caused longer blocking on cache sync ops, which pushed batching windows and increased p99.

pm-jordan: action items for postmortem?

eng-ml-luke: short list:
- add gateway prefix length guard and opt-in truncation for long prompts (>8k) with clear warning to customers
- add per-customer KV cache quota and proactive eviction policy when quota exceeded
- build detection rule for "long-repeat-prefix + high concurrency" to auto-apply routing to smaller model variants
- runbook update: include routing override commands and recommended throttles

sre-raj: infra task: evaluate host memory pressure thresholds that trigger kvcache persistence to disk (avoid hot eviction cycles).

pm-jordan: schedule 1hr postmortem tomorrow 1600 UTC with eng-runtime, eng-ml, SRE, support, and the customer success owner. I'll DM invites.

oncall-amber: leaving handoff to @sre-raj for L2 monitoring, @eng-runtime-mia will follow up on runbook edits. I'll stay on-call until 21:30 then hand to night shift.

incident-bot: Incident INC-3034567890 status: mitigated -> monitoring. paging closed to oncall-amber.

support-ash: I'll follow up with Delia to confirm resolution tomorrow and collect any remaining logs.

eng-runtime-mia: saving collected traces + kvcache stats to internal ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-3034567890 (attachments: trace_21-04_node32.log, kvcache_dump_21-04.json)

sre-raj: marking for follow-up during maintenance window: consider increasing kvcache memory pool for dedicated-nyc-1 if repeated.

pm-jordan: thanks everyone. good coordination. we'll keep the ticket open until postmortem and customer signoff. :thumbsup:
